model.name: Currency / Monetary Value
model.purpose: Attach an exact, governed monetary value - amount, currency, valuation context and precision - to a host record, together with the authority, lifecycle, provenance, protection, retention and interoperability controls that make the attachment auditable and exchangeable.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-032 is a composable mixin. It carries (a) the exact value semantics of a monetary amount: signed decimal amount, currency identified by ISO 4217 alphabetic and numeric code, declared scale/minor-unit handling and a referenced rounding policy; (b) the valuation and conversion context: measurement or valuation instant, rate source reference, rate observation time, measurement basis and functional/presentation currency roles; and (c) the governance controls over that assertion: advisory accountable roles, change authority, weak host-dependent identity, versioning and supersession, normative reference pins, provenance of original and derived values, evidence integrity and audit references, sensitivity classification and access scoping attributes, retention/legal hold/tombstone declarations, and regional/accounting profile and mapping declarations. The mixin never owns its host, the currency register, the rate feed, the reporting framework, the authorization runtime, the records-disposal system or the audit trail.
in_scope: Exact amount representation: signed decimal amount, declared scale, minor-unit handling and a reference to the governing rounding policy version
Currency identification by ISO 4217 alphabetic and numeric code, including fund and historic code status, with the code-list edition and amendment pinned
Valuation and conversion context: valuation/measurement instant, rate source reference, rate observation time, measurement basis and functional/presentation currency roles
Advisory accountable roles for the assertion: accountable value owner, currency-data steward, valuation authority, preparer, independent reviewer, approver
Authority declarations for amount correction, currency and rate-source selection, and rounding-policy change
Weak host-dependent identity of the monetary assertion and the conditions for minting a Dimension-assigned surrogate identifier
Version, effective interval, correction and supersession of the monetary assertion on its host
Provenance of original and derived values, including derivation activity, attributed agent and applied rate
Evidence integrity declarations and references to external audit or assurance records, with stated limitations
Sensitivity classification, commercial restriction and access-scoping attributes published for an external decision point
Retention class, legal-hold flag, disposition readiness and tombstone content for this model's own records
Regional and accounting profile declarations and interoperability mappings with declared losses
out_of_scope: Lifecycle of a currency itself - creation, replacement or withdrawal of ISO 4217 codes is owned by the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency
Operation of exchange-rate feeds, benchmark administration or market-data acquisition
Fair-value measurement methodology, hierarchy classification and reporting-framework disclosure obligations, which belong to the reporting framework
Payment execution, settlement, posting, journal entries, ledger balances and tax determination
The host record's own lifecycle (invoice, contract, order, transaction, account, instrument, price or tariff)
Runtime authorization: policy decision, enforcement, obligation discharge and access-request evaluation
Storage, evaluation or interpretation of audit trails and audit conclusions
Execution of destruction or transfer of records, and the legal decision to impose or release a hold
Non-monetary quantities and units of measure, which belong to a quantity mixin

boundary_notes.distinction: This model pins the code, numeric code, minor unit and list edition it resolved; the register owns code creation, replacement, withdrawal and amendment publication.

This model publishes resource, subject-relevant and environment attributes plus declared scopes; the decision point evaluates policy and the enforcement point applies the result and discharges obligations.
This model declares retention class, trigger, hold flag and tombstone content and assesses disposition readiness; the records system executes disposal, transfer and destruction evidence.
This model records the rate source reference, the instant the rate refers to, the retrieval time and any publisher-stated usage limitation; the publisher owns rate determination and republication.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Financial reporting framework (IAS 21 translation, IFRS 13 fair value)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records which basis and rate were applied and the profile that mandated them; the framework owns the measurement requirement, hierarchy and disclosure.
This model carries a reference to an audit record and a limitation note; the auditor owns evidence sufficiency, testing and conclusions.
XBRL is one projection in which the value becomes a fact bound to a concept, context and unit; this model owns the semantic assertion, not the instance document rules.
This model shapes its lineage fields to PROV entity/activity/agent relations as an alignment; the provenance store owns graph persistence, query and inference.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Jurisdictional tax and statutory conversion rules
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records which statutory conversion rule was applied and its precedence; the tax model owns liability determination and filing.
The parent frames economic value and its reporting context; this mixin narrows to the monetary binding attached to a host record.

sources.title: Global Financial Data Standards - ISO 4217 Currency Codes (Maintenance Agency)
sources.version_or_date: ISO 4217:2015 Maintenance Agency lists (List One current currencies and funds, List Two fund codes, List Three historic codes); consulted 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Normative registry for currency alphabetic code, numeric code and minor unit; establishes the amendment mechanism that requires code-list version pinning and historic-code handling.

sources.title: IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
sources.relevance: Defines functional currency, presentation currency, spot and closing rate, exchange difference and monetary items; grounds valuation instant, rate selection and the original-versus-translated value distinction, including estimation when a currency is not exchangeable.

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement
sources.relevance: Establishes measurement date, observable versus unobservable input hierarchy and disclosure of valuation techniques; grounds valuation authority, measurement basis and input-quality declarations while keeping methodology outside this model.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies entity/activity/agent, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, wasRevisionOf and generatedAtTime as the alignment target for original-versus-derived value lineage and role attribution.

sources.title: Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) 2.1
sources.relevance: Monetary facts are identified by concept, context (entity and instant/duration period) and unit, with optional @decimals/@precision accuracy statements - direct evidence for host-dependent weak identity and for declared numeric accuracy.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Separates policy decision from enforcement and defines subject/resource/action/environment attribute categories, obligations and advice; fixes the boundary that this model supplies attributes only and never renders or enforces decisions.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-162, Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Defines authorization as evaluation of subject, object, operation and environment attributes against policy; grounds publishing object attributes (sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling label) as the model's only access contribution.

sources.title: RFC 3339 - Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Fixes the timestamp profile: full date and time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z, and the distinct meaning of -00:00 for an unknown local offset.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Structures the electronic records lifecycle as capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting with Must Have / Should Have classification; grounds retention metadata and the separation of disposition readiness from disposal execution.

sources.title: 17 CFR 240.17a-4 - Records to be preserved by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers
sources.organization: U.S. Government Publishing Office / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.version_or_date: Code of Federal Regulations, 2024 edition, Title 17, Volume 4
sources.relevance: Sets three- and six-year preservation periods, requires either non-rewriteable non-erasable preservation or an audit-trail alternative recording each modification, and requires records to stay readily accessible to examiners - the strongest constraint on correction-by-supersession.

sources.title: Taxable amount - VAT Directive 2006/112/EC (Article 91 currency conversion)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
sources.version_or_date: Consolidated VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, Article 91; page consulted 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Shows a statutory rate-source mandate with Member State options (most representative market rate, latest ECB published rate subject to notification, or customs-value rules) - direct evidence that rate-source selection is jurisdictional and must be recorded per profile.

sources.title: Euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.version_or_date: Daily publication around 16:00 CET on TARGET working days; consulted 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Documents rate determination by daily concertation around 14:10 CET and publication around 16:00 CET, and states the rates are published for information purposes only with transaction use strongly discouraged - grounds rate observation time and mandatory usage-limitation notes.

sources.title: AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sources.version_or_date: AS 2201, as amended by PCAOB Release No. 2024-005, effective 15 December 2026
sources.relevance: Requires controls over authorization, review and approval of significant transactions and period-end adjustments, notes limits on segregating duties in smaller entities and states that inquiry alone is insufficient evidence - grounds advisory role and segregation declarations and their evidence expectations.

bundles.name: Authority, accountability and monetary assertion lifecycle
bundles.description: Who may assert, correct or re-base a monetary value on its host, how that assertion is identified without an independent identity, and how it is versioned, made effective, corrected and superseded against pinned normative references.
bundles.rationale: Authorization of transactions and review/approval of period-end adjustments are control objectives in their own right (SRC-013), while the identity of a monetary fact is derived from concept, context and unit rather than from a standalone key (SRC-005). Currency code lists change by published amendment (SRC-001) and mandated rate sources differ by jurisdiction (SRC-011), so version pinning belongs with lifecycle rather than with representation.

layers.name: Accountable roles and change authority
layers.description: Advisory declarations of who is accountable for a monetary value and who is competent to change its amount, its currency, its rate source or the rounding policy applied to it.

findings.name: Accountable roles and segregation of duties
findings.description: Declaration of the parties associated with a monetary assertion - accountable value owner, currency-data steward, valuation authority, preparer, independent reviewer and approver - and of whether those positions are held by distinct parties. All declarations are advisory metadata; no permission is granted or withheld here.

questions.text: Which party is recorded as accountable for this monetary value on its host record, and over what interval?
Which function stewards the currency code list and rounding configuration, and which body is named as the valuation authority for the basis applied?
Are preparer, independent reviewer and approver held by distinct parties for this assertion?
Under which declared rule may one party hold more than one of these positions, and what compensating declaration is then recorded?
What evidence supports each declared role assignment where the reviewer relied on an automated check rather than re-performance?

data_elements.name: Accountable party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party recorded as accountable for the monetary value on its host; optional, because no source requires a single owner for every monetary value.

data_elements.name: Role assignment entry
data_elements.description: An advisory association of a party with one role (steward, valuation authority, preparer, reviewer, approver) over an effective interval, shaped for PROV attribution and delegation.

data_elements.name: Segregation relief declaration
data_elements.description: Recorded rule reference, combined positions and compensating measure where duties cannot be segregated, as anticipated for smaller or less complex entities.

data_elements.name: Review and approval state
data_elements.description: Observable state code for the review and approval position of the assertion, so that approval is never inferred from the mere presence of a value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role and segregation declarations are structured reference data pointing at party records held elsewhere; they carry no rendered content of their own and produce no document. Materialising them as artifacts would duplicate the party register and imply that this model holds the authoritative personnel record, which it does not.

findings.name: Authority for amount correction, currency and rate-source selection, and rounding policy
findings.description: Declaration of the authority under which an existing amount or currency may be corrected, under which a rate source is chosen, and under which the rounding and minor-unit policy applied to the value may be changed - including whether that authority is jurisdictional or entity-internal.

questions.text: Which authority record permits a correction to the amount or currency of an existing monetary assertion?
On what basis was the exchange-rate source selected, and is the selection mandated by a jurisdictional rule or chosen under entity policy?
Which rounding and minor-unit policy version applies, and who is competent to change it?
What is recorded when the mandated rate source publishes nothing for the required instant or the currency is not exchangeable at the measurement date?

data_elements.name: Change authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authority record (delegation, policy or statutory rule) relied on for a correction or re-basing of the value.

data_elements.name: Rate-source selection basis
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing a statutorily mandated source, a framework-required spot or closing rate, and an entity-policy choice.

data_elements.name: Rounding policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference plus version of the rounding and minor-unit policy applied; the ISO 4217 minor unit is an input to that policy, not the policy itself.

data_elements.name: Rate fallback declaration
data_elements.description: Record of the substitute source, estimation basis or deviation applied when the mandated source or an exchange rate was unavailable.

artifacts.name: Monetary change-authority declaration
artifacts.description: A dated statement naming the authority relied on for amount correction, rate-source selection and rounding-policy change, with its scope and expiry. It records authority; it does not evaluate or enforce it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier of the issuing governance system's policy or delegation record; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID.

layers.name: Assertion identity, versioning and normative pins
layers.description: How a monetary assertion is identified through its host, how its versions and effective intervals are managed, and which external code-list and policy versions were in force when it was made.

findings.name: Host-dependent weak identity of a monetary assertion
findings.description: A monetary value has no independent existence: it is identified by its host record, the role it plays on that host, its currency and its valuation context, mirroring how a reported monetary fact is identified by concept, context and unit. A valuation date is context, never an identifier.

questions.text: Which combination of host reference, role on the host, currency and valuation context uniquely identifies this monetary assertion?
Under which conditions must the adopting Dimension mint a surrogate identifier instead of relying on the host key?
How is this assertion distinguished from another that merely carries the same amount and the same currency?
Is the monetary assertion an inseparable component of the host record or a separately addressable record?

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record the monetary value is attached to; mandatory because the mixin has no standalone existence.

data_elements.name: Role on host
data_elements.description: Code for the position the value occupies on its host (for example gross amount, tax amount, translated amount), which discriminates same-valued siblings.

data_elements.name: Identity component set
data_elements.description: Ordered list naming the attributes that jointly identify the assertion (host reference, role, currency, valuation context), used for collision checks.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned surrogate identifier
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID minted only when the host key is unavailable or unstable; never derived from a date.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity here is a key definition and a set of pointer fields evaluated at read time. Emitting an artifact would create a second, competing identity anchor for something that is deliberately dependent on its host, and would invite systems to treat the monetary value as an independent master record.

findings.name: Version, effective interval, correction and supersession
findings.description: Lifecycle verbs govern the monetary binding on its host - asserted, revised, superseded, withdrawn - and never the currency, the rate feed, the transaction, the account or the instrument. Where preservation rules forbid rewriting, correction is expressed as an additive superseding version.

questions.text: Which lifecycle states may a monetary assertion occupy on its host, and which transitions between them are permitted?
How are the interval over which the asserted value is effective and the instant at which it was recorded represented separately?
When a corrected amount is issued, is the prior assertion overwritten or retained as an immutable superseded version?
Which external record must be cited when the change is driven by an event this model does not own, such as a restatement or a re-issued source document?

data_elements.name: Assertion status
data_elements.description: State of the monetary binding on its host (for example asserted, superseded, withdrawn); scoped to the binding, not to any external object.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: Start and optional end of the interval over which the asserted value holds, expressed with explicit offsets.

data_elements.name: Recorded-at timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion was recorded in the holding system, kept distinct from the valuation instant and from the rate observation time.

data_elements.name: Superseded assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a corrected assertion to the version it replaces, aligned with a provenance revision relation.

data_elements.name: External change trigger reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally owned record that occasioned the change; this model records the pointer, not the external record's own lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Monetary assertion revision note
artifacts.description: A per-revision note recording what changed, the authority cited, the trigger and the superseded version, retained additively so that no prior value is erased.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Host key plus role plus zero-padded monotonic revision sequence; the sequence number never encodes a date.

findings.name: Currency-list and policy version pins
findings.description: Record of which ISO 4217 code-list edition and amendment, and which rounding, rate-source and accounting-profile policy versions, were in force when the assertion was made - so the value stays interpretable after those references change. The register's own lifecycle stays with its maintenance agency.

questions.text: Which ISO 4217 code-list edition and amendment number were in force when this currency code was resolved?
How does a value citing a withdrawn or replaced currency code remain interpretable after the register publishes the replacement?
Which policy versions - rounding, rate-source rule and accounting profile - are pinned to this assertion?
How is a pin recorded when the referenced register or policy publishes no version identifier?

data_elements.name: Currency code-list pin
data_elements.description: Edition, amendment number and list identifier of the ISO 4217 code list used to resolve the currency, with the resolution time.

data_elements.name: Currency code status
data_elements.description: Whether the cited code is current, a fund code or a historic code under the maintenance agency's published lists.

data_elements.name: Policy version pin
data_elements.description: Reference and version label of each governing policy in force at assertion time, plus a content digest when the source is unversioned.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Pins are short structured references whose authoritative content lives in externally published lists and policy registers. Copying those lists into local artifacts would fork a normative register that the maintenance agency alone may amend, and would create stale duplicates of material this model must only cite.

bundles.name: Provenance, protection, retention and interoperability of monetary context
bundles.description: How an original or derived monetary value is attributed and evidenced, how its confidentiality and access scopes are declared, how long the context is kept and what survives disposition, and how it is mapped to external representations under regional and accounting profiles.
bundles.rationale: Derivation, attribution and delegation relations are standardised (SRC-004); rate publishers attach explicit usage limitations that must travel with the value (SRC-012); preservation format and accessibility duties apply to financial records (SRC-010) within a lifecycle whose disposal step belongs to the records programme (SRC-009); and access decisions are made by an external decision point from published attributes (SRC-006, SRC-007).

layers.name: Value provenance and evidence integrity
layers.description: Lineage from original to derived monetary values, attribution of responsibility, and the integrity and limitations of the evidence that supports them.

findings.name: Provenance of original and derived monetary values
findings.description: Lineage of a monetary value: which original amount it came from, which conversion, translation, re-measurement or allocation produced it, which rate was applied and for which instant, and which agent is responsible - shaped to entity/activity/agent provenance relations.

questions.text: From which original value, by which activity and with which applied rate was this derived monetary value produced?
Which agent is attributed responsibility for the derived value, and on whose behalf did that agent act?
Which instant does the applied rate refer to, and when was it retrieved from its publisher?
Is the recorded value an as-transacted amount, a translated amount or a re-measured amount?
What tolerance is accepted between a value recomputed from the lineage and the stored value?

data_elements.name: Original value reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the as-stated monetary value from which this value was derived; absent when the value is itself original.

data_elements.name: Derivation activity
data_elements.description: Type, parameters and time of the activity that produced the derived value (conversion, translation, re-measurement, allocation).

data_elements.name: Applied rate source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the publisher and series of the rate applied, together with any publisher-stated usage limitation.

data_elements.name: Rate reference instant
data_elements.description: The instant the applied rate refers to, distinct from the instant the rate was retrieved and from the recorded-at time.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis
data_elements.description: Code stating whether the amount is as transacted, translated at a spot or closing rate, or re-measured on another basis.

data_elements.name: Attributed agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent responsible for producing the value, with optional delegation to the agent it acted on behalf of.

artifacts.name: Conversion lineage record
artifacts.description: A record binding the original value, derivation activity, applied rate, rate instant and attributed agent so that a derived value can be independently recomputed and challenged.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived assertion key plus derivation activity identifier; falls back to a Dimension-assigned ULID where the activity is unidentified.

findings.name: Evidence integrity, audit references and stated limitations
findings.description: Integrity declarations for the evidence supporting a monetary value (rate snapshots, source documents, approval records), references to external audit or assurance records, and explicit limitations - including that a rate published for information only cannot be presented as a transaction rate. This model holds neither the audit trail nor the audit conclusion.

questions.text: Which integrity check value and algorithm are recorded for each evidence item supporting this value?
How is the completeness of the evidence set for a monetary assertion checked declaratively?
Which limitation must be stated when the supporting rate is published for information purposes only?
What is recorded when evidence is missing, superseded, or supplied by a party with an interest in the value?
Which external audit or assurance record is cited, and what does this model deliberately not assert about it?

data_elements.name: Evidence item entry
data_elements.description: Reference, kind and origin of one item of supporting evidence for the monetary assertion.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest value and algorithm recorded for an evidence item, supporting later detection of modification without asserting that any control operated.

data_elements.name: External audit record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to an audit or assurance record concerning the value or its controls; the reference conveys existence and scope only.

data_elements.name: Evidence limitation note
data_elements.description: Statement of the declared limits of an evidence item, such as a publisher's information-only qualification on a reference rate.

artifacts.name: Rate evidence snapshot
artifacts.description: A captured copy of the rate quotation relied on, with publisher, series, reference instant, retrieval time and any usage limitation as published.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Rate source identifier plus series plus rate reference instant, with a zero-padded capture sequence for repeated captures of the same instant.

artifacts.name: Evidence integrity manifest
artifacts.description: A manifest listing each evidence item with its digest, algorithm and computation time, enabling recomputation and comparison without altering the evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assertion key plus manifest revision reference; no date component is used as the identifier.

layers.name: Sensitivity classification and access scoping
layers.description: Confidentiality classification of monetary values and the attributes and scopes this model publishes so that an external decision point can evaluate a request.

findings.name: Sensitive or commercially restricted values and access scopes
findings.description: Classification of monetary values that are commercially restricted or otherwise sensitive, the handling labels that must travel with them, and the declaration of access constraints at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope. The model contributes attributes only; decision and enforcement remain with the external authorization component.

questions.text: Which sensitivity class applies, and does it attach to the amount, the currency, the counterparty or the derivation?
Which values are commercially restricted such that disclosure would breach a contractual confidentiality term?
Which resource and environment attributes must this model expose so that an external decision point can evaluate a request?
How is a required masked, banded or rounded projection of a restricted amount declared without asserting that masking has been applied?
Which time-bounded exceptions permit broader access, for example to a regulator or an external auditor?

data_elements.name: Sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Classification code for the monetary value, used as an object attribute by an external decision point.

data_elements.name: Commercial restriction basis
data_elements.description: Code and agreement reference explaining why the value is commercially restricted.

data_elements.name: Declared access scope
data_elements.description: The scope at which an access constraint is declared: bundle, layer, finding or artifact.

data_elements.name: Handling label
data_elements.description: Label that must accompany the value when projected into another system, carried as advisory metadata.

data_elements.name: Access exception declaration
data_elements.description: Time-bounded declaration of a broader-access basis, such as regulatory examination access to preserved records.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are attribute declarations consumed at request time by an external policy decision point; they have no standalone rendered form. Producing an artifact would encourage the model to be treated as a policy store or as the record of an access decision, which would take ownership of evaluation and enforcement that belong to the authorization component.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and profile interoperability
layers.description: How long monetary context and its evidence are kept, what survives disposition, and how the value is declared against regional and accounting profiles and mapped to external representations.

findings.name: Retention class, legal hold and tombstone
findings.description: Declaration of the retention class and trigger for this model's own monetary context records and evidence, the presence and source of a legal hold that suppresses disposition, and the tombstone content retained after disposal. Disposal execution, transfer and destruction evidence belong to the records programme.

questions.text: Which retention class, trigger event and minimum period apply to this monetary context record and its evidence?
How is a legal hold recorded so that disposition is suppressed, and which external authority issued it?
Which end-of-life states may the record occupy, and which fields survive in a tombstone after disposal?
Which system executes disposal, and what does this model record as evidence that disposition occurred?
How are retention obligations reconciled when the host record and the monetary assertion carry different periods?

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Classification assigning the monetary context record to a retention schedule owned by the records programme.

data_elements.name: Retention trigger event
data_elements.description: The event that starts the retention clock, such as record creation or closure of the host transaction.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Boolean declaring that disposition is suppressed; the decision to impose or release the hold is made outside this model.

data_elements.name: Hold authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instruction or authority under which the hold was imposed.

data_elements.name: Tombstone content
data_elements.description: The minimal surviving record after disposal: assertion key, host reference, currency code, retention class, disposition time and disposition record reference, with amount and evidence removed.

data_elements.name: Disposition record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally held record evidencing that disposal was carried out.

artifacts.name: Monetary context tombstone record
artifacts.description: The surviving stub for a disposed monetary context record, preserving identity and disposition facts while carrying no amount or evidence content.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The assertion key of the disposed record, preserved unchanged so that inbound references resolve to a tombstone rather than dangling.

findings.name: Regional and accounting profile declaration and interoperability mappings
findings.description: Declaration of the regional, tax or accounting profile that governs a value - including functional and presentation currency roles and statutory conversion rules - and of the mappings to external representations, each labelled as an alignment or an evidenced conformance claim, with declared losses.

questions.text: Which regional, tax or accounting profile governs this value, and which currency roles does it assign?
To which external representations is this monetary context mapped, and is each mapping an alignment or a claim of conformance?
Where the external representation cannot express a local field, what loss is declared and what round-trip behaviour is expected?
Which rule takes precedence when two profiles mandate different rate sources for the same underlying value?
Which checks must pass before a conformance claim, rather than an alignment, may be recorded?

data_elements.name: Governing profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference and version of the regional, tax or accounting profile governing the value's currency roles and conversion rule.

data_elements.name: Interoperability mapping entry
data_elements.description: Pairing of a local field with a field in an external representation, labelled as alignment or conformance.

data_elements.name: Declared mapping loss
data_elements.description: Statement of information that cannot survive a mapping, such as pins or limitation notes with no target field.

data_elements.name: Profile precedence rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule resolving competing profile mandates, or an indicator that two mandated values must coexist.

artifacts.name: Profile conformance statement
artifacts.description: A statement naming the profile, its version, the checks performed and whether the result is an alignment or an evidenced conformance claim.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile reference plus profile version plus the identifier of the model release the statement was made against.

artifacts.name: External representation mapping table
artifacts.description: A field-level mapping table between this model's monetary context and an external representation, including unmapped fields and declared losses.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Target representation identifier plus target version; a Dimension-assigned ULID is used when the target publishes no version.

functions.name: Check accountable role completeness
functions.description: Compare the declared role assignments for a monetary assertion against the role set required by its governing profile and report missing or expired assignments.
preconditions: The assertion carries a host reference and a role on host
A governing profile version is pinned or a default profile is declared
effects: Emits an advisory report only; assigns no permission, blocks no operation and creates no obligation

functions.name: Check segregation of duties declarations
functions.description: Test whether preparer, independent reviewer and approver references are distinct parties and, where they are not, whether a relief declaration with a compensating measure is present and unexpired.
preconditions: Party references resolve to distinguishable identifiers
Relief rules are declared with an effective interval
effects: Produces a declarative finding; does not decide whether the control is effective and does not stand in for audit testing

functions.name: Resolve the effective monetary assertion
functions.description: Given a host reference, a role on host and a point in time, return the assertion version whose effective interval covers that point, together with its status and any superseding version.
preconditions: Effective intervals and recorded-at timestamps are present with explicit offsets
At most one non-superseded version covers the requested point
effects: Read-only resolution; writes nothing and does not alter status

functions.name: Check currency-list and policy pins
functions.description: Verify that the currency code-list pin and policy version pins are present and resolvable, and flag a code that has become historic or been replaced relative to the pinned list.
preconditions: Read access to the published code-list edition named in the pin
Policy references expose a version label or a content digest
effects: Reports drift between pinned and current references; never amends the register and never changes the stored currency code

functions.name: Verify provenance chain completeness
functions.description: Check that a derived monetary value carries an original value reference, a derivation activity, an applied rate with its reference instant and retrieval time, and an attributed agent, and report which links are absent.
preconditions: The value is declared as derived rather than original
Timestamps are expressed with explicit offsets
effects: Emits a completeness report; performs no market-data retrieval and does not re-derive the value

functions.name: Verify evidence integrity against manifest
functions.description: Recompute digests for referenced evidence items and compare them with the recorded integrity manifest, reporting mismatches, missing items and unrecorded additions.
preconditions: Evidence items are readable at their recorded references
The manifest records algorithm and computation time for each entry
effects: Reports discrepancies without remediating, quarantining or deleting evidence; does not constitute audit evidence of control operation

functions.name: Derive published access attributes
functions.description: Compute the object attribute set and declared scopes that an external decision point consumes, from sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels and access exception declarations.
preconditions: A sensitivity class is declared or a default class is pinned by the governing profile
effects: Publishes attributes only; renders no permit or deny decision, enforces nothing and discharges no obligation

functions.name: Assess disposition readiness
functions.description: Determine whether the retention period computed from the trigger event has elapsed, whether any legal hold is active, and whether the host record's period is longer, and report an eligibility outcome.
preconditions: A retention class and trigger event are declared
Hold status is current at evaluation time
effects: Advisory readiness assessment only; the records programme executes disposal, transfer and destruction and owns the disposition record

functions.name: Report profile conformance and mapping loss
functions.description: Check mapping completeness against a named external representation and emit an alignment or conformance report listing mapped fields, unmapped fields and declared losses.
preconditions: The target representation version is identified or a content digest is recorded
Required checks for a conformance claim are declared
effects: Records an alignment by default and a conformance claim only where the declared checks pass and are evidenced; asserts nothing about the external system's behaviour

composition.purpose: Places the monetary binding within the parent's treatment of economic value and reporting context; the parent frames what is being valued, this mixin governs the monetary assertion attached to a host.

composition.target: Host record model of the adopting Dimension (entity, event or document that carries the amount)
composition.purpose: Supplies the host reference, role on host and context period on which the mixin's weak identity depends; the host retains its own lifecycle and identity.

composition.target: ISO 4217 currency code register maintained by the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency
composition.purpose: Resolves the alphabetic code, numeric code, minor unit and code status, and supplies the edition and amendment number to pin. Code creation, replacement and withdrawal remain with the register.

composition.target: External authorization component (policy decision and enforcement points)
composition.purpose: Consumes the published sensitivity, restriction and scope attributes and renders and enforces access decisions. This model never evaluates a request or discharges an obligation.

composition.target: Records management and disposition authority (retention schedules and disposal execution)
composition.purpose: Owns the retention schedule, disposal execution, transfer and destruction evidence; this model declares class, trigger, hold and tombstone content and assesses readiness only.
Shapes original-versus-derived lineage, agent attribution, delegation and revision relations to standard provenance terms without adopting provenance graph storage, query or inference.

composition.target: Financial reporting framework model (IAS 21 translation, IFRS 13 fair value measurement)
composition.purpose: Aligns currency roles, spot and closing rate use and measurement basis vocabulary; measurement methodology, hierarchy classification and disclosure obligations remain with the framework.

composition.target: XBRL business reporting projection (monetary fact, unit and context)
composition.purpose: Maps the assertion to a fact bound to a concept, context and unit with a declared accuracy attribute, as one projection of the semantics held here.

composition.target: Exchange-rate publication and market-data source registry
composition.purpose: Identifies the rate publisher, series, reference instant and any publisher-stated usage limitation. Rate determination, publication schedule and republication remain with the publisher.

composition.target: Jurisdictional tax and statutory conversion rule model
composition.purpose: Supplies the mandated conversion rule and any notification duty for a given jurisdiction and transaction class; tax liability determination and filing remain outside this model.

composition.target: External audit and assurance record model
composition.purpose: Carries a citation and a scope limitation for an audit record touching the value or its controls; evidence sufficiency, testing and conclusions remain with the auditor.

composition.target: Temporal expression profile for internet timestamps
composition.purpose: Fixes how valuation instants, rate reference instants, retrieval times and recorded-at times are written, including the distinct meaning of an unknown local offset.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an owner package that holds the model specification, the pinned currency code-list edition reference and the governing rounding, rate-source and profile policy references, and publishes their version labels.

The owner package declares which external components own authorization decisions, records disposition and audit records, and records those bindings as resolvable references before the model is used in production.

The owner package publishes the identifier scheme used for Dimension-assigned surrogate identifiers and the party register that role references resolve against, and states that role assertions are advisory.
The owner package records the regional and accounting profiles in force, including competing rate-source mandates, and the precedence rule or the decision to carry dual values.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers are lower-kebab-case and prefixed for this model; they must not embed dates, amounts or currency codes. External vocabularies are referenced by their own governed identifiers - ISO 4217 codes by the maintenance agency's code with the list edition pinned, provenance terms by the PROV namespace IRI - and are never re-minted in a local namespace. Where a Dimension must mint an identifier, it uses a UUID or ULID under a namespace it controls and records the minting reason.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-032 (model WM-XCT-032), parent WM-ECO-004
ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency currency code lists (current, fund and historic) as the referenced register
W3C PROV namespace http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# as the provenance alignment target

canonicalization_rules: Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds present and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is preserved as meaning an unknown local offset and is never rewritten to Z.

Currency codes are canonicalised to the uppercase alphabetic code with the numeric code carried alongside, and the code-list edition and amendment that resolved them are pinned rather than assumed current.
References are canonicalised to their authoritative identifier form; display names, labels and human-readable notes are excluded from any canonical form used for digests.
Digest inputs are canonicalised by sorting object keys, omitting absent optional fields and excluding the digest field itself, so that recomputation is deterministic across projections.
patch_rules: A change to amount, currency, applied rate, measurement basis or effective interval is a superseding version that cites the prior version and a change authority; where non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative applies, in-place overwriting is prohibited.

A change to advisory metadata (handling labels, non-normative notes, mapping documentation) may be applied in place, and the recorded-at timestamp is updated while the effective interval is left unchanged.
A patch must not alter a pinned code-list edition, amendment number or policy version retroactively; re-pinning is recorded as a new assertion version with its own recorded-at time.
A patch that removes a field required by a governing profile is rejected and reported rather than applied silently.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field, a new sensitivity class value or a new mapping entry is backward compatible; consumers ignore unknown optional fields.

Narrowing a cardinality, making an optional field required, or changing the meaning of a status or class code is breaking and requires a new model version and a re-issued profile conformance statement.
Historic currency codes remain valid in stored assertions after the register withdraws them; consumers must resolve them against the historic list rather than reject them.
A conformance claim against an external representation is invalidated when that representation's version changes and reverts to an alignment until the declared checks are re-run.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record that owns the artifact or the host record it belongs to (for example the accounting or document system's record key), used whenever it exists and is stable.

Governed global identifier or IRI: an identifier from a governed external scheme, such as a maintenance-agency currency code with its pinned list edition or a namespace IRI, used where the artifact references externally governed content.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, minted only when neither of the above exists, with the minting reason recorded.

Composite weak key of host reference, role on host, currency and valuation context, used for resolution and collision detection but never as a substitute for a stable identifier when one is available.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are written in RFC 3339 form with seconds always present and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is reserved for an unknown local offset and is not equivalent to Z. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they can differ: the valuation or measurement instant and the rate reference instant are event times, while the rate retrieval time, the recorded-at time and any digest computation time are observation or ingestion times. A date without a time of day may be recorded only where the governing profile defines the value as a whole-day event, and a date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by their stable parent key followed by a zero-padded monotonic sequence number that carries no date, amount or currency component - revision notes as assertion key plus revision sequence, and rate evidence snapshots as rate source and series plus the rate reference instant plus a capture sequence for repeated captures. Sequence numbers are never reused after supersession or disposal.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact records a digest value, the algorithm used and the digest computation time in an integrity manifest, computed over the canonical form. Corrections are additive superseding versions rather than edits, so that a modification history remains reconstructable where non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative is required. Verification reports discrepancies only; it never repairs, quarantines or deletes evidence, and it is not a substitute for audit testing.

policies: Role, authority and segregation declarations are advisory metadata. An external authorization component owns every allow or deny decision, and no monetary value is presumed to have an owner or a valuation authority unless one is declared.

Lifecycle verbs in this model act on the monetary binding on its host. They never create or imply a lifecycle for a currency, a price, a rate feed, a transaction, an account or an instrument; where such a change is the cause, an external record is cited instead.

Rate and valuation inputs are recorded with their source, reference instant, retrieval time and any publisher-stated usage limitation; a rate published for information purposes only is never presented as a transaction rate.
Pinned references govern interpretation. A stored assertion is read against the code-list edition and policy versions pinned at assertion time, not against the current ones.

Conformance to an external standard is claimed only where declared checks have been run and evidenced; otherwise the relationship is recorded as an alignment, and known conflicts are recorded rather than reconciled by assumption.

read: Reads resolve the effective assertion for a host reference, role and point in time, returning the version whose effective interval covers that point together with its status and any superseding version.
Reads return pinned code-list and policy versions alongside the value so that a consumer can interpret a historic currency code or a superseded rounding policy correctly.

Reads of restricted values return the published attribute set and any declared projection constraint; the decision to release, mask or band the value is made and applied by the external authorization component.
Reads never mutate status, hold flags or retention state, and read access to preserved records must remain available to an entitled examiner for the duration of the retention period.
create: Creation requires a resolvable host reference and a role on host; a monetary assertion is never created without a host.
Creation records the recorded-at time and, where the value is derived, the original value reference, derivation activity, applied rate, rate reference instant and rate retrieval time.
Creation pins the currency code-list edition and amendment and the governing rounding, rate-source and profile policy versions, or records a content digest where the source publishes no version.
Creation may record advisory role assignments and a sensitivity class; absence of an owner or approver is represented explicitly rather than defaulted.
update: A change to amount, currency, applied rate, measurement basis or effective interval creates a superseding version citing the prior version, a change authority and, where applicable, the external record that triggered it.
In-place modification is prohibited wherever non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative applies; the modification history must remain reconstructable.
Advisory metadata may be updated in place with a refreshed recorded-at timestamp, leaving the effective interval and pins untouched.
An update that would violate a pinned policy version or remove a profile-required field is rejected and reported, not silently coerced.
delete: Records of this model are never hard-deleted while their declared retention period is unexpired or a legal hold flag is active; the hold suppresses disposition until the issuing authority releases it.

On expiry of the retention period with no active hold, the record becomes disposition-eligible and is reduced to a tombstone that preserves the assertion key, host reference, currency code, retention class, disposition time and disposition record reference, while the amount, lineage detail and evidence content are irreversibly removed.
The tombstone retains the original assertion key so that inbound references resolve to a disposed marker rather than dangling; keys are never reused.

Execution of disposal, transfer and physical destruction, and the disposition record evidencing it, are owned by the adopting Dimension's records management authority under its retention schedule and by the applicable preservation rule for financial records. This model only assesses readiness, declares the tombstone content and stores the reference to the externally produced disposition record.
Where the host record's retention period is longer than the assertion's, the longer period governs and the record remains undeletable until the reconciled eligible-from time.

roles.name: Accountable value owner
responsibilities: Is recorded as accountable for a monetary value on its host and for the correctness of its declared context
Confirms the governing profile and the sensitivity class applied to the value
Requests correction through the declared change authority rather than editing a preserved value

roles.name: Currency-data steward
responsibilities: Maintains the pinned currency code-list edition and amendment reference and the handling of historic, fund and replaced codes
Maintains the rounding and minor-unit policy reference and its version label
Reports drift between pinned and currently published register content without amending stored assertions retroactively

roles.name: Valuation authority
responsibilities: Names the rate source and measurement basis permitted for a class of values under a profile
Records the fallback basis when a mandated source publishes nothing or a currency is not exchangeable
Records the publisher-stated usage limitations that must travel with a cited rate

roles.name: Preparer
responsibilities: Creates the monetary assertion with its host binding, valuation context, lineage fields and pins
Attaches the supporting evidence items and their digests
Declares explicitly where required context is unavailable rather than defaulting it

roles.name: Independent reviewer
responsibilities: Checks the assertion against its governing profile, pins and lineage completeness
Records the review outcome as an observable state and the evidence relied on, distinguishing automated checks from re-performance
Records a segregation relief declaration and compensating measure where positions overlap

roles.name: Approver
responsibilities: Records approval of the assertion or of a superseding correction under a cited change authority
Confirms that the correction mode complies with the applicable preservation rule
Does not act as preparer for the same assertion unless an unexpired relief declaration is recorded

roles.name: Records custodian
responsibilities: Maintains the retention class, trigger and hold flags for monetary context records and their evidence
Consumes disposition readiness reports and links the externally produced disposition record
Ensures preserved records remain accessible to entitled examiners for the retention period

roles.name: Access administrator
responsibilities: Maintains the mapping from sensitivity class and restriction basis to the attributes published for the external decision point
Registers time-bounded access exception declarations and their bases
Confirms that this model publishes attributes only and holds no decision or enforcement logic

access.default_rule: Deny by default at every scope. This model publishes object attributes, declared scopes and projection constraints; an external policy decision point evaluates each request against subject, resource, action and environment attributes, and an enforcement point applies the result and discharges any obligation. Nothing recorded here grants access by itself.
exceptions: Regulatory or supervisory examination access to preserved monetary records and their evidence, recorded as a time-bounded exception citing the preservation rule that requires ready accessibility.
External auditor access to evidence items and approval records for a defined engagement period, recorded with the engagement reference and an explicit non-transfer condition.
Counterparty-facing disclosure of a commercially restricted amount only where the restricting agreement permits it, with the permitted recipient class and interval recorded.
Break-glass access under a named authority, recorded with the requesting party, the justification, the interval and a mandatory post-hoc review reference.
Artifact-scope exception for a tombstone record, which remains resolvable after disposal because it carries no amount or evidence content.
audit_requirements: Each declared access exception records its basis reference, beneficiary class, interval and the party that registered it, so that the declaration itself is reviewable.
Attribute changes affecting release - sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels - are versioned with a recorded-at timestamp and the party that made them.

This model records references to externally held access and audit logs and their scope limitations; it does not store, evaluate or interpret the access log or the audit trail, which remain owned by the authorization and audit components.
Where an access exception expires or is released, the release time is recorded rather than the declaration being deleted, so the historical basis stays reconstructable.

required_fields: Pinned currency code-list edition and governing policy versions
Externally owned components: authorization decision point, records disposition authority, audit record source
Boundary statement: advisory roles only, no enforcement, no external lifecycle ownership
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any other artifact.
Read the Specification URL to load the model boundary, in-scope and out-of-scope statements and the boundary notes, so that target-owned concepts are not re-implemented locally.

Read the Storage type URL to learn how the format-neutral structure is projected into the concrete store, then the Interface URL for the read, create, update and delete contracts including the tombstone rule.
Read the Processes URL for the declarative check functions, then resolve the pinned currency code-list edition and policy versions before creating or interpreting any monetary assertion.

Resolve the externally owned components last and confirm their bindings; if the authorization decision point or the records disposition authority cannot be resolved, operate in read-only mode and report the gap.

coverage.claim: This structure grounds the authority, accountability, identity, lifecycle, provenance, evidence, protection, retention and interoperability controls of a monetary value in primary standards from twelve independent organisations: the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency for currency code identification and amendment pinning, the IFRS Foundation for currency roles, rate basis and measurement, W3C PROV for derivation and attribution, XBRL for the weak identity of a monetary fact, OASIS and NIST for the attribute-only access boundary, IETF for timestamp form, NARA and the CFR preservation rule for retention and correction-by-supersession, the European Commission and the ECB for jurisdictional rate-source mandates and publisher limitations, and PCAOB for authorization, review and segregation expectations. Amount and currency representation and valuation context are declared in the model boundary and carried by the identity, pin, lineage and measurement-basis elements defined here. The claim is falsifiable: every structural node cites a retrieved source, and unsupported material is recorded as a gap rather than presented as canonical.

checklist.notes: Weak host-dependent identity grounded in the identification of a monetary fact by concept, context and unit; surrogate identifiers are conditional, and a valuation date is explicitly excluded as an identifier.

Lifecycle verbs act only on the monetary binding on its host - asserted, revised, superseded, withdrawn - with correction-by-supersession where non-rewriteable preservation applies. No lifecycle is created for a currency, rate feed, transaction, account or instrument.

Host mix-in, parent economic model, currency register, rate publisher, authorization component, records authority, audit record and reporting framework are all expressed as composition links with explicit ownership boundaries.

Effective interval, valuation and rate reference instants (event time) are separated from rate retrieval, recorded-at and digest computation times (observation time); all use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, and -00:00 retains its distinct meaning.
Original-versus-derived lineage, derivation activity, applied rate and instant, agent attribution and delegation are aligned to PROV terms; a recomputation tolerance is declared.
Accountable value owner, currency-data steward and valuation authority are advisory and optional; no source supports a universal owner, so absence is represented explicitly rather than defaulted.

Declarative checks cover role completeness, segregation distinctness, pin resolution, provenance completeness, evidence integrity and conformance-claim preconditions; none of them decides control effectiveness.
Attribute-only contribution with deny-by-default, four declared scopes and time-bounded exceptions; decision, enforcement and obligation discharge are explicitly outside the model.

Retention class and trigger, legal-hold suppression, disposition readiness assessment, tombstone content and key preservation are declared; disposal execution and the disposition record are owned by the records authority and the applicable preservation rule.
Profile declaration, mapping entries labelled alignment or conformance, declared losses, historic-code interpretation and precedence between competing rate mandates are all represented.

Separate authority declarations for amount correction, rate-source selection and rounding-policy change, distinguishing statutory mandate from entity policy, with a fallback path when a mandated source is unavailable.
Preparer, reviewer and approver distinctness is tested declaratively with an explicit relief-and-compensating-measure path, reflecting that smaller entities may be unable to segregate duties.

Digest, algorithm and computation time per evidence item, a manifest, defect and interested-party flags, publisher usage limitations, and audit references carried with an explicit non-assertion statement.

Sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels and projection constraints are declared as object attributes; whether a monetary value constitutes personal data is left to a referenced privacy model.

Rate source, reference instant, retrieval time, measurement basis and currency roles are recorded, with a fallback for non-exchangeability; measurement methodology and hierarchy classification stay with the reporting framework.
A monetary assertion has no intrinsic geometry. Jurisdiction is handled as a profile and precedence question rather than as a spatial property.

known_omissions: The ISO 20022 repository could not be retrieved during this research; its ActiveCurrencyAndAmount constraints (total and fraction digits, currency attribute) are recorded as an unverified alignment and must be validated before any payments-message mapping is claimed.

ISO 4217:2015 and ISO 15489-1:2016 texts are behind paywalls and were not retrieved; currency code semantics were grounded in the maintenance agency's published lists and records-lifecycle structure in the NARA requirements instead.
US GAAP ASC 830 was not consulted, so the model records no evidence about its differences from IAS 21 on translation and remeasurement.
Hyperinflationary-economy restatement (IAS 29) and its interaction with valuation-date semantics are not represented.
Benchmark administration governance, such as the EU Benchmarks Regulation, was not verified; rate-source governance is treated only as a reference and a selection basis.
Non-ISO-4217 units of account - crypto-assets, loyalty points, vouchers, commodity-denominated units - are unresolved; the code-list pin assumes an ISO 4217 code space.
No cryptographic non-repudiation scheme (signature or trusted timestamping profile) is specified for approvals; only digest-based integrity is declared.
conflicts: The ECB publishes euro reference rates for information purposes only and strongly discourages transaction use, while the VAT Directive permits the latest published ECB rate for converting a taxable amount. A rate can therefore be legally mandated in one context and disclaimed by its publisher in another; the limitation note must travel with the value and must not be generalised into permission.

IAS 21 requires translation at the spot rate at the transaction date for the functional currency, while VAT Article 91 allows a Member State market rate, the ECB rate or customs-value rules. One economic event can carry two differently converted mandated amounts; the model records both with their profiles rather than reconciling them.

The ISO 4217 minor unit is a code-list attribute, not a rounding mandate. Statutory or contractual rounding may differ, so rounding is expressed as a pinned policy reference and never inferred from the minor unit.

A monetary fact identified only by concept, context and unit conflicts with master-data practice that expects a stable standalone identifier. This is resolved as weak host-dependent identity with conditional surrogates, which will break systems that assume a global monetary-value key.

Non-rewriteable preservation or audit-trail requirements for financial records conflict with in-place correction patterns common in operational systems; the model forces additive supersession, which increases storage and complicates naive last-write-wins synchronisation.

PCAOB expectations for segregated authorization, review and approval conflict with the practical staffing of smaller entities, so the model must permit an explicit relief declaration rather than assume full segregation.
regional_assumptions: EU rate-source rules are treated as one profile among several: Member States may mandate the most representative market rate, permit the latest published ECB rate subject to notification, or apply customs-value rules for defined categories.

US broker-dealer preservation periods and non-rewriteable or audit-trail requirements are treated as a jurisdiction-specific profile, not as a universal retention rule; other jurisdictions impose different periods.
The NARA electronic records lifecycle structure is used as a general lifecycle reference; it is a US federal programme requirement and is not binding outside that context.
IFRS is assumed only where a profile declares it; local GAAP profiles may assign different currency roles, rate bases and disclosure duties.
Currency code lists change by published amendment, so any assumption that a stored code is currently valid is jurisdiction- and time-dependent and must be resolved against the pinned edition.
No single global tax or accounting profile is assumed; precedence between competing profiles is an explicit decision recorded per value.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a normative requirement that every monetary value has an owner or a valuation authority. None was found, so role assignment is modelled as optional advisory metadata with explicit absence, rather than as a mandatory field that would fabricate accountability.

Tested whether the ISO 4217 minor unit can be presented as a rounding rule. The maintenance agency publishes it as a code-list attribute alongside alphabetic and numeric codes, so a rounding mandate was rejected and rounding was demoted to a pinned external policy reference.

Tested whether this model may hold audit conclusions or an audit trail. Audit evidence sufficiency and conclusions rest with the auditor and access logs rest with the authorization component, so only references and explicit non-assertion statements are carried; no audit-trail storage, evaluation or retention semantics are modelled locally.

Checked whether ECB reference rates could be treated as authoritative transaction rates. The publisher discourages transaction use, so rate-source declarations were required to carry a usage limitation instead of an implied permission.

Attempted to justify a local disposition workflow with destruction steps. The records lifecycle places disposal execution with the records programme, so only a readiness assessment, a hold declaration and a tombstone for this model's own records were retained.

Attempted to justify local access-decision logic so that restricted amounts could be masked by the model. Decision and enforcement are separated from attribute publication in both the access-control standard and the ABAC guide, so the model publishes attributes and declared projection constraints only and never records that masking occurred.

Tested whether a valuation date could serve as an identifier for repeated valuations of the same host amount. It cannot discriminate two valuations at the same instant from different sources, so identity was defined over host reference, role, currency and valuation context with a conditional surrogate.

Reviewed every bundle, layer, finding and function against each composition rationale for target-owned concepts. Rate determination, register amendment, measurement methodology, payment and posting, authorization evaluation, disposal execution and audit-trail semantics were all pushed to out-of-scope entries, boundary notes or reference links rather than modelled here.
